name: Daksh Adhikari
description: Mechanical engineering PhD student at Georgia Tech working on flow-boiling instabilities and active control.
summary:

academicProjects.title: Two-Phase Flow Boiling
academicProjects.description: Flow-boiling experiments use pressure measurements and machine learning to detect unstable operation and guide active control toward a stable operating range.
academicProjects.longDescription:
Flow boiling removes high heat loads, but pressure-drop and density-wave oscillations can make a cooling loop hard to operate. The work applies to electronics thermal management, EV batteries, high-energy lasers, and nuclear cooling.

At Georgia Tech's MiNDS Lab with Dr. Satish Kumar, pressure measurements feed a machine-learning control framework. The measurements distinguish stable from unstable operation without optical access, and the classification guides active flow control.

Stable and unstable regimes have different probability-density functions and spectral content. Unstable operation shows dispersed distributions and low-frequency oscillations from 0–5 Hz. Stable operation has sharper, leptokurtic distributions with dominant frequencies near 50 Hz. A 2.5-second sampling window balances signal stability against detection latency. In a proof-of-concept demonstration, manual actuation moved the loop from an unstable regime back to a stable operating point.

Related publication:

- Adhikari, D.; & Kumar, S. "Mitigation of Flow Boiling Instabilities via Active Flow Control." IEEE Intersociety Conference on Thermal and Thermomechanical Phenomena in Electronic Systems (ITherm), 2026.

academicProjects.title: Rapid Cooling for Neutron Sample Environments
academicProjects.description: Rapid-cooling hardware and controls for neutron sample environments cut a key helium-cooled furnace cooldown from over two hours to under five minutes; an LN2-cooled sample stick reached about 80 K in under two minutes.
academicProjects.longDescription:
High-temperature neutron furnaces often rely on radiation cooling after an experiment, so the 500–100 °C part of cooldown can take more than two hours. Dry cryostats commonly need about two hours to cool a room-temperature sample to roughly 80 K.

At Advanced Cooling Technologies, the DOE SBIR Phase II-A program covered day-to-day development, reporting, and presentations. The resulting closed-loop, low-pressure helium system has automated controls and a new in-situ cooling feature. It was demonstrated during a live neutron experiment at ORNL's VULCAN beamline; the demonstration raised the technology readiness level to 8 and supported a patent filing.

For low-thermal-mass furnace cases with no sample, helium circulation reduced the 500–100 °C cooldown from over two hours to under five minutes. With a high-thermal-mass sample, automated cooling reduced the interval by a factor of over 20, and the system cooled from 1500 to 100 °C in under 12 minutes during in-situ neutron diffraction. The cryostat sample stick used an embedded liquid-nitrogen transport line; preliminary tests reached approximately 80 K in under 2 minutes, compared with about 2 hours for a dry cryostat.

A separate average-Nusselt-number correlation used helium, nitrogen, argon, and a nitrogen–helium mixture. Its maximum deviation from measured values was 15.7%, with more than 66% of points within ±5%.

academicProjects.title: Swiss-Roll Combustor
academicProjects.description: Open-source CFD models supported low-flow flare combustor designs, including a Swiss-roll geometry for lean methane combustion with limited NOx; a later fuel-injection revision addressed flashback risk.
academicProjects.longDescription:
Small oil and gas sites use flares to combust methane, but low-flow operation can reduce destruction efficiency. Texas reported about 97,000 flares in 2017; roughly one third operated below 20 MSCFD.

At Advanced Cooling Technologies, open-source CFD models covered fluid flow, heat transfer, and combustion. They were used to evaluate and optimize a compact Swiss-roll combustor for low-production sites. The work was presented at the American Flame Research Committee symposium and the ARPA-E Summit.

A Swiss-roll is a spiral counterflow heat exchanger around the combustion chamber. Hot products preheat incoming reactants, which extends the flammability range for lean, low-flow methane while keeping effective peak temperatures low enough to limit thermal NOx. The 2023 enclosed design targeted high methane destruction and ultra-low NOx. The 2024 revision moved fuel injection near the combustion zone instead of premixing at the inlet, addressing flashback and auto-ignition risk under fluctuating flow.

Related publications:

- Adhikari, D.; Bhuripanyo, P.; Rao, P.; Radyjowski, P.; Chen, C.-H.; & Ronney, P. "Swiss-roll Combustor: An Innovative Enclosed Combustor for high Methane Destruction Efficiency and Ultra-low NOX Emissions." American Flame Research Committee Industrial Combustion Symposium, Denver, 2023.
- Radyjowski, P.; Lieberknecht, E.; Adhikari, D.; Rao, P.; Chen, C.-H.; Bhuripanyo, P.; & Ronney, P. academicProjects.title: Predicting Cooling Performance of Dimpled Channels
academicProjects.description: A study at Advanced Cooling Technologies used neural networks to predict heat-transfer coefficient and pressure drop in water-cooled dimpled ducts from CFD data.
academicProjects.longDescription:
Dimpled ducts can improve heat transfer, but evaluating each geometry with CFD is slow and established correlations are limited for these shapes.

This study at Advanced Cooling Technologies used a fully connected artificial neural network to predict the hydrothermal performance of water-cooled dimpled ducts from a limited CFD-generated dataset. The inputs and outputs were used without an existing correlation between them.

For dimpled-duct geometries held out from training, the model predicted heat-transfer coefficient within ±17% and pressure drop within ±19% of simulated values. The result supports screening candidate geometries before full CFD or experiments.

Related publication:

- Shaeri, Mohammad Reza; Randriambololona, Andoniaina M.; & Adhikari, Daksh. "Machine Learning Algorithm for Predicting Heat Transfer Coefficient and Pressure Drop in Dimpled Ducts." ASME Heat Transfer Summer Conference, 2024.

academicProjects.title: Uncertainty-Aware Drug-Target Binding Prediction
academicProjects.description: A graph-neural-network pipeline for drug-target affinity prediction combines a five-seed uncertainty estimate with ranking that can abstain on low-confidence candidates.
academicProjects.longDescription:
Drug-target screening needs both a ranking of candidate compounds and a way to flag predictions that may be unreliable. This project combines affinity prediction with uncertainty-aware, budget-constrained ranking and was built for the GT STAR-AI Makerspace Hackathon on May 12, 2026.

Three model families were compared: a small pretrained pair (ChemBERTa + ESM-2 35M), a large pretrained pair (ChemBERTa-large + ESMC-600M), and a task-specific graph isomorphism network (GIN) trained from scratch on 94,115 kinase binding pairs. The GIN used a five-seed deep ensemble; disagreement between ensemble members supplied the uncertainty estimate. A multi-agent RAG layer supported biomedical reasoning and decision support.

The GIN achieved concordance indices of 0.882 on KIBA, 0.735 on Davis, and 0.625 on out-of-distribution BindingDB, compared with 0.856/0.861, 0.655/0.665, and 0.587/0.580 for the pretrained comparisons. It won 49 of 53 KIBA kinase subfamilies. Mean uncertainty rose 2.75× from in-distribution (σ̂=0.121) to out-of-distribution data (σ̂=0.333); abstention AUROC was 0.760, and budget-constrained screening recovered 72 of the top 100 binders at the p99 threshold. The task-specific ensemble identified high-error predictions best, while the large pretrained ensemble had the lowest ECE at 0.015. Experiments ran on a Mac Mini M4, taking 3–6 hours per seed.

The associated paper is submitted, not accepted.

Related publication:

- Adhikari, D.; et al. "Uncertainty-Aware Drug-Target Affinity Prediction with Budget-Constrained Compound Ranking." IEEE International Conference on Biomedical and Health Informatics (BHI), 2026 (submitted).

academicProjects.title: GelMA Granular Hydrogel Scaffolds
academicProjects.description: A Penn State study examined how centrifugal packing of GelMA microparticles changes scaffold pores, mechanics, and cell behavior in vitro and in vivo.
academicProjects.longDescription:
Granular hydrogel scaffolds are made by packing hydrogel microparticles and bonding them at their contacts. The packing state controls pore architecture and the mechanical environment available to cells.

This multi-institutional Penn State study used external centrifugal force to deform and pack gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) microparticles. Increasing force or duration increased packing, decreased void fraction and median pore diameter, and increased compressive and storage moduli. MDA-MB-231 human triple-negative breast adenocarcinoma cells spread and flattened in loosely packed scaffolds but became elongated under the spatial confinement of highly packed scaffolds. In mouse subcutaneous implants, lower-packing-density scaffolds showed greater endothelial, fibroblast, and macrophage infiltration. The study also examined non-muscle myosin II-driven contractility using blebbistatin-treated cells.

The contribution was as an undergraduate researcher in Penn State's Bio-Soft Materials Laboratory.

Related publication:

personalProjects.title: MyPantryChef
personalProjects.description: An iPhone cooking app that suggests recipes from ingredients on hand, adapts them to preferences, and guides cooking with step-by-step timers.
personalProjects.longDescription:
The prototype tracks pantry ingredients through manual entry or photos. Recipe ideas use dietary preferences, exclusions, and serving size; plain-English requests handle changes such as “no butter” or “make it spicier”.

Recipes can be imported from a URL or a handwritten-recipe photo, scaled, saved, and revisited. Cook mode shows one instruction at a time, with progress tracking and timers.

personalProjects.title: Agent CAD — From a Description to a 3D Model
personalProjects.description: A workflow for AI agents to turn descriptions, dimensions, and reference files into editable CAD models on a local computer.
personalProjects.longDescription:
Parts are modeled in code, so dimensions and individual components can be revised without rebuilding an assembly by hand. Both the geometry and modeling code stay local.

The gallery contains two reference-assisted guitar studies: a GT partscaster and a dual-humbucker Epiphone Les Paul. The partscaster accompanies [the physical guitar build](/projects/guitar-partscaster-build-and-onboard-effects).

personalProjects.title: Guitar: Partscaster Build & Onboard Effects
personalProjects.description: A partscaster with Fuzz Face-style fuzz and a treble booster built into the guitar, ahead of the wireless transmitter.
personalProjects.longDescription:
Placing the effects before the wireless transmitter preserves the interaction between the pickups and the circuits’ low input impedance. A body switch selects fuzz, boost, or bypass.

The electronics use 500K pots, a single-point star ground, and a switching output jack that disconnects the battery when the cable is unplugged.

![Breadboarding the onboard fuzz and treble-booster circuit](/guitar-wiring-breadboard.jpg)

personalProjects.title: Pixel Sentinel — Repurposed Android Security Camera
personalProjects.description: An old Pixel 3a XL turned into a private security camera, with live video, two-way audio, snapshots, and recording in a browser.
personalProjects.longDescription:
The phone runs IP Webcam, with a Python proxy connecting it to a custom browser interface over Tailscale. Video and push-to-talk are available without a separate camera-app login.

The setup supports snapshots, recorded clips, and spoken guard-mode announcements. A watchdog restarts the stream if it stops.

personalProjects.title: Local-business website demos
personalProjects.description: Responsive website demos for local businesses with missing or outdated sites, built from their public listings, photos, services, and reviews.
personalProjects.longDescription: The workflow researches a business category, finds local prospects, and gathers material from their listings, existing websites, and social pages. An AI-assisted editor uses that material to build a working HTML demo, with service information, photos, attributed reviews, and contact links.
